HSTU aggregates values using SiLU(QKᵀ + positional/temporal bias), followed by normalization and gating; attention weights are not softmax probabilities. Deletion changes available evidence and aggregation, while compacting survivors also changes relative positional distances. Meta’s reference implementation divides attention by padded attention width, so changing that width introduces another confound; deleting events within a fixed-width input leaves this divisor unchanged. Temporal bias uses bucketed time differences with shifted query timestamps corresponding to next-event prediction; arbitrary item–timestamp misalignment therefore changes attention independently of item order. These details are implementation-specific and must be checked against the supplied backbone. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152), [official implementation](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/hstu.py).

Architecture-compatible controls, inferred from these mechanisms: compare compacted deletion against explicitly masked removal retaining original position coordinates and surviving timestamps; match recent versus older deletions by event count and retained length. Hold padded width, candidates, prediction time and readout convention fixed. For shuffling, distinguish permuting item identities across fixed timestamp slots from permuting complete item–timestamp pairs: the former tests content ordering under a fixed timeline; the latter also alters temporal structure and may violate chronology. Keep the final observed item fixed in a separate control, since moving or deleting it changes the readout token itself. With LEFT padding, always select the final nonpadding position, never count−1. Recompute perturbed histories without stale caches, disable dropout, and report paired validation score/rank changes by history length. Interpret effects as model sensitivity to these interventions—not proof of causal recency preference or unobserved user traits.
